independent_saved_source_review.reviewer: Separate assistant review of saved source passages, claims and raw facts; no additional external model or network calls.
independent_saved_source_review.conclusion: No clear unsupported delivered financial value or narrative proposition found in these two saved final reports. This limited source-grounding review is not an accuracy measurement.

findings.detail: Eight answers use FY2024, 2023-07-01 to 2024-06-30, with underlying 10-K filed 2024-07-30 and conservative availability 2024-07-31, before cutoff 2024-08-01. Independent calculations reproduce margin 44.64%, FCF 74071000000 USD, FCF margin 30.22%, and capex ratio 18.14%.

The separate model review rejected a draft that reversed the direction of AI infrastructure costs versus margin improvement. The original rejected prose was not preserved; only the rejection reason is available.

The planning question presupposes capex/R&D ratios increased, while the delivered financial table is a single fiscal year. This is a planning hypothesis, not a verified finding; final claims do not repeat the asserted increase.
Five answers use FY2026, 2025-01-27 to 2026-01-25, and the 2026-02-25 10-K, available 2026-02-26. Independent ratios reproduce operating margin 60.38% and R&D ratio 8.57%.

The claim includes export-control risk but its two attached short quotes cover supply, estimation, and capital. The cited DOC_2 selected full text separately contains explicit export-control disruption language, so the proposition is supported at document level; attach that sentence as an additional quote for a complete claim-level citation.

The DOC_1 quote ends mid-clause at “higher material”. The other cited DOC_2 full text supports higher costs and gross-margin risk, so the conditional interpretation is not contradicted. Prefer complete-sentence quotations to make the evidentiary link reviewable.

The saved model review reason renders $59.3 billion as 59.3亿美元 rather than 593亿美元. The delivered claim contains no amount and its verbatim source quote is correct. This illustrates why model review explanations are not a numeric accuracy oracle.
